title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 79
paragraphs: He said this thinking to give pleasure; but Pausanias answered him: “Stranger of Aegina, I admire your friendly spirit and your forethought for me, but you have missed a good opinion nevertheless; for after exalting me and my family and my deed, you then cast me down to nothing by advising me to commit an outrage on a dead body, and by saying that if I do this I will be better reported of. Such things are more fitting for barbarians than for Greeks — and even in barbarians we find fault with such deeds. However that may be, I do not wish to please, in any such way as this, either Aeginetans or others who delight in such things. It is enough for me that I keep free of unholy deeds — yes, and of unholy speech too — and so please the Spartans. As for Leonidas, whom you bid me avenge, I declare that he has been greatly avenged already, and honored by the countless lives taken of these men — and not only he, but also the rest who ended their lives at Thermopylae. As for you, do not come to me again with such a proposal, nor give me such advice; and be thankful, moreover, that you go unpunished for it now.”
